issues.text: Unlisted claim: the definition gives a cause no claim in the ledger asserts, and it is false as a general rule. `echo` is a builtin (`type -t echo` -> builtin) and changes no shell state; so are `true`, `printf` and `[`. The lesson contradicts itself two paragraphs later: "`pwd` and `echo` are two more the shell can do itself". A reader who takes the definition literally must conclude echo changes the shell.
issues.quote: built-in — something the shell carries out itself instead of starting a program, because it changes the shell's own state.
issues.fix: Drop the false cause and keep it a definition: "built-in — something the shell carries out itself instead of starting a program; `cd` has to be one, because only the shell can change where the shell stands."

issues.text: `>` is not "handed over" at all, changed or otherwise. Execution: `printf '[%s]\n' a b > f` wrote exactly `[a]` and `[b]` into f — neither `>` nor the file name arrived as an argument. The lesson's own ledger says so (claim 19: "`>` sends the output to a file instead of reaching the program as an argument"), so the body states the opposite of the claim it is supposed to render, and plants a model foundation.l1.pipes-and-filters must break.
issues.quote: you will meet words like `*` and `>` that the shell does change before handing them over
issues.fix: Write: "you will meet words like `*`, which the shell replaces with the names of the files it matches before handing them over, and `>`, which it keeps for itself to send the output to a file."

issues.text: False for the output printed right above it, in the one section that tells the reader to "match the output to the lines that produced it". A reader who does the matching exercise carefully ends with two lines that have no `echo` to belong to.
issues.quote: `echo` with nothing after it prints an empty line — the blank lines in the output are that, not decoration.
issues.fix: Write: "`echo` with nothing after it prints an empty line — the blank lines between the blocks are that, not decoration; the two inside the listing are `ls` separating one folder's group from the next." Update claim 11 in .meta.json to the same wording.
